Andy Jassy’s AI Advice for Young People: Learn It, Keep Thinking

28 Oct 2026, 10:19 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

Image: timesofindia.indiatimes.com — Creative Commons

Share this article
WhatsAppFacebookTelegram
Key takeawaysAndy Jassy encourages young people to learn and experiment with AI, while retaining human judgment and original thinking. The article summarizes his reported advice and its limits.

Navigating the AI Revolution

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy is encouraging younger generations to integrate artificial intelligence into their professional and academic lives, rather than attempting to avoid the rapidly evolving technology. In a recent interview on 'The a16z Show,' Jassy emphasized that the era of AI-integrated education and work is permanent, urging students and early-career professionals to actively experiment with these tools.

Jassy, whose own children are in their early twenties, noted that the academic landscape has shifted significantly since the emergence of generative AI. He observed that attempts by institutions to restrict the use of AI in classrooms are likely futile. Instead, he advocates for a proactive approach: learning the technology and using it as a foundational element for day-to-day productivity.

The Role of AI in Productivity

According to Jassy, AI offers a clear advantage by automating tedious preliminary tasks—what he describes as 'grunt work.' He highlighted academic research, note-taking, and information gathering as areas where AI can help individuals reach an 'advanced starting spot' more efficiently.

Jassy shared that neither of his children are professional software developers, yet they have utilized AI tools to build functional applications, illustrating how the technology lowers the barrier to entry for creative and technical invention. He encourages young people to explore these capabilities, even if they are outside their traditional areas of expertise.

A Warning on Over-Reliance

Despite his advocacy for AI adoption, Jassy issued a cautionary note regarding the limitations of the technology. He warned that AI-generated writing often lacks a cohesive quality, noting that it is frequently easy to distinguish from human-authored work.

'I still think you’re going to need human judgment and ingenuity and invention and experimentation and thinking about how all the pieces come together,' Jassy said. He emphasized that while AI can assist in the process, the human capacity for critical thinking remains essential for building successful businesses and meaningful user experiences. For Jassy, the goal is not to let AI replace original thought, but to use it as a scaffold for higher-level innovation.
